meta.name: KTHQ Acquisition Package Preflight Rules
meta.thresholdNotes: Ordinary simplified acquisition threshold treated as $350,000. FAR 13.5 commercial simplified procedures treated as up to $9,000,000, or $15,000,000 for listed contingencies/emergencies.
meta.schemaNotes: Required rule fields: id, section, severity, matches or any, title, explanation. Optional fields: scoreImpact, capScore, phase, cite, concierge, fixWith, clearedBy, evidence. phase can be stop, funding-authority, requirement-doc, research-justification, surveillance-admin, or risk-flags.

rules.title: Dollar range is unknown
rules.explanation: Most Preflight checks calibrate to dollar thresholds like the MPT, SAT, and FAR 13.5. Without a rough band, the tool cannot apply several important rules.
rules.concierge: You do not need an exact number yet, but the package should know whether this is tiny, under the SAT, above the SAT, or a large action.

fixWith.label: Funding and Color of Money Helper
fixWith.description: Help frame funding and rough order of magnitude.

rules.title: Fiscal year posture is unknown
rules.explanation: For an above-SAT package, the file should know which fiscal-year funds are expected and whether timing creates an obligation or bona fide need issue.
rules.concierge: The CO does not need the full accounting string to start, but the package should know the funding year story.

fixWith.label: Funding and Color of Money Helper
PALT Builder
fixWith.description: Connect funding timing to acquisition milestones.

rules.title: Recompete has no fresh market research
rules.explanation: A recompete should not rely only on the old contract file. Refresh the market, incumbent context, pricing, set-aside potential, and vehicle options before locking the strategy.
rules.concierge: A follow-on may feel familiar, but the market and the requirement can both change between awards.

rules.title: Recurring need has no vehicle strategy yet
rules.explanation: For recurring above-SAT work, consider whether a schedule, BPA, IDIQ, or other existing vehicle fits before defaulting to a standalone action.

fixWith.label: Blanket Purchase Agreements
fixWith.description: Review BPA fit for repeat buys.

rules.title: Long T&M/LH period increases surveillance risk
rules.explanation: A long time-and-materials or labor-hour period needs extra attention to ceiling, surveillance, funding, and whether a lower-risk structure would work.
rules.concierge: Long-running T&M work can quietly drift if the ceiling and surveillance plan are weak.

fixWith.label: Cost and Price Analysis
fixWith.description: Review contract type and pricing risk.

rules.title: Services action has no requirement document
rules.explanation: For a services acquisition above the SAT, the package needs a structured requirement path before solicitation: PWS, SOW, or SOO. Without it, offerors cannot price or perform against a coherent need.
rules.concierge: A service buy needs to say what the contractor must accomplish, how success will be measured, and what the Government will inspect.

clearedBy.label: Select PWS, SOW, or SOO under Requirement document status.

evidence: PWS, SOW, or SOO approved by the requiring activity
Clear scope, tasks, performance standards, and deliverables
Government review notes showing the requirement is ready for acquisition
Attachments or exhibits referenced by the requirement document

fixWith.label: PWS Builder
fixWith.description: Build a complete performance work statement.

rules.title: Service requirement document exists
rules.explanation: You have a PWS, SOW, or SOO path selected. That gives the CO something concrete to evaluate before solicitation.

rules.title: Supply buy lacks specs or purchase description
rules.explanation: For supplies or equipment, the package should describe the minimum need through specs, salient characteristics, drawings, or a purchase description. Otherwise you risk unclear quotes and accidental brand lock-in.
rules.concierge: Industry needs enough detail to know what counts as acceptable, without the Government quietly writing around one preferred product.

rules.title: IGCE has not started on an above-SAT action
rules.explanation: This is a serious package gap. The estimate supports funding, price analysis, negotiation posture, and acquisition planning. Treat this as a fix-before-solicitation item unless your local process has a documented alternate path.
rules.concierge: The IGCE is the Government's own estimate. It helps you know whether the proposed price later makes sense.

clearedBy.label: Move IGCE status to in progress or complete.

evidence: IGCE or rough-order estimate with assumptions
Basis for quantities, labor categories, materials, and rates
Source data used to estimate price or cost
Reviewer or customer approval, if required locally

fixWith.label: Cost and Price Analysis
fixWith.description: Review price analysis and cost-estimate concepts.

rules.title: IGCE is complete
rules.explanation: A completed IGCE gives the file a cost baseline for funding and price-reasonableness work.

fixWith.label: Price Fair and Reasonable
fixWith.description: Connect the estimate to later price analysis.

rules.title: Sole-source path lacks a ready justification
rules.explanation: A restricted action above the SAT needs the correct justification path moving before solicitation. If the package says one source but the justification is not started or is unsure, the acquisition approach is not ready.
rules.concierge: If you are not competing, the file must explain why competition is not available or not required under the chosen authority.

clearedBy.label: Move the justification to in progress or complete.
Use a competitive approach if the facts support competition.

evidence: Draft or approved J&A, LSJ, brand-name justification, or fair-opportunity exception
Market research showing available sources and why alternatives do or do not meet the need
Authority citation and approval path
Facts supporting the restriction, not just conclusions

fixWith.label: Evaluating Justifications
fixWith.description: Review J&A, LSJ, and restricted-competition logic.

fixWith.label: Other Than Full and Open Competition

rules.title: Justification document is complete
rules.explanation: The restricted-competition record is already built, which should reduce review churn if the facts and authority line up.

fixWith.label: Evaluating Justifications
fixWith.description: Check the justification against common weaknesses.

rules.title: Brand-related buy lacks salient characteristics
rules.explanation: Brand-name and brand-name-or-equal packages need documented minimum characteristics. Without them, the file cannot explain what equal means or why the named item is necessary.
rules.concierge: Do not just name the product. Explain the features the Government actually needs.

clearedBy.label: Document salient characteristics or minimum specifications.

evidence: Minimum salient characteristics or specifications
Explanation of why each characteristic matters to the requirement
Market research showing whether equivalent products can meet the need
Brand-name or brand-name-or-equal justification, if required

rules.title: Brand-related salient characteristics are only partial
rules.explanation: Partial characteristics are a start, but the package should clearly distinguish minimum needs from preferences before solicitation.

rules.title: IDIQ path needs fair-opportunity documentation
rules.explanation: If this is an IDIQ order and you plan to limit sources or skip fair opportunity, the file needs the applicable exception and documentation before release.
rules.concierge: An IDIQ does not mean you can simply pick the contractor. The ordering rules still matter.

fixWith.label: Exceptions to Fair Opportunity
fixWith.description: Review FAR Part 16 fair opportunity exceptions.

rules.title: Need date is inside 30 days and funding is not ready
rules.explanation: This is a schedule-risk pairing. A near-term need with incomplete funding usually needs immediate PALT triage and an honest conversation with the customer.
rules.concierge: The fastest way to miss a need date is to pretend funding timing is not part of acquisition timing.

fixWith.label: Funding and Color of Money Helper

rules.title: Near-term need has no market research
rules.explanation: A package with a close need date and no market research is likely to lose time later. Start the research record before the schedule becomes the justification.

fixWith.label: Market Research Tool
fixWith.description: Pull public market data and build a memo.

fixWith.label: Market Research
fixWith.description: Learn the market research file logic.

rules.title: Market research is not started
rules.explanation: Market research informs commerciality, competition, set-aside potential, pricing context, and vehicle selection. Not starting it early usually creates rework.
rules.concierge: Market research is not just a memo. It is how you learn whether the requirement and acquisition strategy make sense.

clearedBy.label: Conduct market research and move the status to formal or informal.

evidence: Sources checked and dates searched
Vendors or products identified with capability notes
Set-aside analysis and small business consideration
Commerciality notes and vehicle options
Price references or prior-award context
Market research recommendation or memo

fixWith.label: Market Research Tool
fixWith.description: Search public sources and generate a memo.

rules.title: Formal market research is complete
rules.explanation: A formal market research record gives the acquisition strategy a factual base.

rules.title: COR not identified for a requirement that likely needs surveillance
rules.explanation: For services, construction, mixed performance, or Government-site work, identify the surveillance owner early. Waiting until award creates avoidable administration risk.
rules.concierge: If no one is assigned to watch performance, the contract may be easy to award and hard to manage.
evidence: COR nomination or designation documentation
COR training status
COR duties tied to the specific contract
Communication plan between CO, COR, and requiring activity

fixWith.label: Contract-Specific COR Training
fixWith.description: Prepare the COR for the actual contract.

rules.title: COR is designated and trained
rules.explanation: A trained COR reduces award-to-performance friction and helps the CO keep the file healthy.

fixWith.label: Annual COR File Reviews
fixWith.description: Keep the COR file healthy after award.

rules.title: COR is named but training is not current
rules.explanation: A named COR still needs current training and contract-specific preparation. Fixing this before award is much easier than reconstructing the file later.

fixWith.label: Contract-Specific COR Training
fixWith.description: Prepare the COR for this requirement.

rules.title: Services requirement lacks a surveillance plan or QASP
rules.explanation: If the Government cannot describe how performance will be assessed, the requirement is not ready for clean administration.
rules.concierge: A QASP is the Government's plan for checking whether the contractor is doing what the contract requires.

clearedBy.label: Create a surveillance plan or QASP draft.

evidence: Surveillance plan or QASP
Performance standards and inspection method
Acceptance process and responsible Government personnel
Reporting cadence and documentation expectations

fixWith.label: PWS Builder
fixWith.description: Build performance standards and surveillance hooks.

rules.title: Surveillance plan exists
rules.explanation: The package has a defined path for inspecting performance after award.

rules.title: Personal services concerns are flagged
rules.explanation: If the contract may create an employer-employee relationship, stop and review the structure before solicitation. This can be a real legal and acquisition strategy problem.
rules.concierge: Contractor personnel should not be managed like Government employees unless the acquisition is authorized as personal services.

clearedBy.label: Resolve the structure so personal services concerns are removed or not applicable.

evidence: Analysis of supervision, direction, and control
Description of contractor independence and deliverable-based work
Legal or policy review if concerns remain
Requirement language revised to avoid unauthorized personal services

fixWith.label: Personal vs. Non-Personal Services
fixWith.description: Learn the supervision and control warning signs.

rules.title: Personal services risk is uncertain
rules.explanation: Uncertainty here deserves review. Clarify supervision, tasking, workspace, and Government control before solicitation.

rules.title: Bona fide need mismatch identified
rules.explanation: A known mismatch between the need and the funds is a stop-and-get-help issue. Do not paper over it with schedule pressure.
rules.concierge: The Government generally must use funds for a legitimate need of the period for which those funds are available.

clearedBy.label: Resolve the fiscal-law issue so the bona fide need posture is yes or not applicable.

evidence: Funding document or resource advisor confirmation
Bona fide need analysis tied to period of performance or delivery
Appropriation type and fiscal year
Legal or fiscal review if the timing is unusual

fixWith.label: Funding and Color of Money Helper

rules.title: Bona fide need posture is unsure
rules.explanation: If you are unsure whether the need matches the funds, clarify before solicitation. This is exactly the kind of issue that becomes painful if discovered late.

fixWith.label: Funding and Color of Money Helper

rules.title: O&M-funded performance crosses fiscal years
rules.explanation: This is not automatically wrong, but it needs deliberate fiscal-law review. Check severability, bona fide need, and period-of-performance structure.
rules.concierge: Annual money and cross-year service periods can be fine, but the file needs to know why.

fixWith.label: Funding and Color of Money Helper

rules.title: Funding and bona fide need posture look clean
rules.explanation: The package says funding is in place and the bona fide need year matches. Keep the supporting documentation in the file.

fixWith.label: Funding and Color of Money Helper
fixWith.description: Use the helper if the funding story changes.

rules.title: Urgency claimed without alternatives analysis
rules.explanation: Urgency can support a faster or restricted path, but the file still needs facts showing what alternatives were considered and why the schedule could not support a normal path.

fixWith.label: Other Than Full and Open Competition
PALT Builder
fixWith.description: Show the schedule pressure in a milestone plan.

rules.title: T&M/LH path lacks ceiling and surveillance approach
rules.explanation: Time-and-materials and labor-hour contracts are higher-risk. The package needs a ceiling and active surveillance logic before solicitation.
rules.concierge: T&M pays for labor hours, so the Government needs a firm ceiling and a real plan to watch the work.

clearedBy.label: Define the T&M/LH ceiling and surveillance approach.

evidence: Ceiling amount and basis
D&F or approval required for T&M/LH use
Surveillance plan showing how hours and deliverables will be monitored
Rationale for why a lower-risk contract type is not suitable

rules.title: High-risk contract type lacks surveillance planning
rules.explanation: T&M, labor-hour, and cost-type work deserve stronger surveillance planning. Build the surveillance approach before the solicitation goes out.

rules.title: IT/cyber terms are not yet understood
rules.explanation: IT requirements often carry Section 508, cybersecurity, access, data, or IP concerns. If the package is unsure, bring technical and clause review in early.
evidence: Section 508 applicability decision
Cybersecurity, access, or hosting requirements
Data rights, IP, or license terms if applicable
Technical reviewer input
Clause/profile assumptions for IT and cyber terms

fixWith.label: Clause Matrix
fixWith.description: Check clause logic once the acquisition profile is clearer.

rules.title: IT/cyber requirement has unusual terms
rules.explanation: Unusual data, IP, access, or cybersecurity terms are manageable, but they need review before solicitation language hardens.

fixWith.label: Clause Matrix
fixWith.description: Review clause logic once the profile is stable.

rules.title: Construction package has not considered bonds/protection
rules.explanation: Construction packages should consider bonding, payment protection, wage, safety, site, and performance requirements before solicitation.

clearedBy.label: Document construction bond or payment protection consideration.

evidence: Bond or payment protection determination
Construction specs, drawings, and site information
Wage determination or labor standards review
Safety, access, and notice-to-proceed assumptions

rules.title: Construction bond/protection considered
rules.explanation: Bonding and protection requirements are already on the radar for the construction package.

rules.title: No PALT plan for a near-term need
rules.explanation: If the need date is inside 90 days, backwards planning should already be visible. Build the milestone plan now, even if it is ugly.

fixWith.label: PALT Builder
fixWith.description: Generate a milestone plan from the acquisition profile.

rules.title: PALT plan built with KTHQ
rules.explanation: You have already backed into the need date using the PALT Builder. Keep that schedule with the package.

fixWith.label: PALT Builder
fixWith.description: Update the schedule if assumptions change.

rules.title: Small business path not considered
rules.explanation: For an above-SAT action, the file should show that small business and set-aside potential were considered, even if the final answer is not a set-aside.

rules.title: Small business path considered
rules.explanation: The package shows small business consideration, which helps support the acquisition strategy.

rules.title: First-time action has not had an independent review
rules.explanation: If the CO or shop is new to this type of action, get another experienced reviewer before solicitation. That review may save days later.

fixWith.label: FAR Research Tool
fixWith.description: Route the issue to the right FAR part.

rules.title: GFP/GFI posture is unsure
rules.explanation: If the Government may furnish property or information, clarify it before solicitation. Access, timing, controls, and clauses can affect performance.

fixWith.label: Clause Matrix
fixWith.description: Check clause implications once facts are known.

rules.title: GFP/GFI involved
rules.explanation: Government-furnished property or information is manageable, but the package should identify what is furnished, when, by whom, and under what controls.

fixWith.label: Clause Matrix
fixWith.description: Check clause implications once facts are known.

rules.title: OCI exposure needs review
rules.explanation: Known or uncertain organizational conflict of interest exposure should be addressed before solicitation. The solicitation may need mitigation, disclosure, or evaluation language.

clearedBy.label: Resolve OCI exposure or document why no OCI concern remains.

evidence: OCI screening notes or analysis
Known relationships, prior work, or access concerns
Mitigation plan, disclosure language, or evaluation approach if needed
Legal or policy review when exposure is material

fixWith.label: Solicitation Builder
fixWith.description: Build solicitation language after the risk is resolved.

rules.title: Public or political sensitivity flagged
rules.explanation: Sensitive buys need a cleaner record, earlier leadership awareness, and more careful public-facing documentation.

rules.title: Commercial path above SAT needs commerciality support
rules.explanation: If using commercial or FAR 13.5 procedures above the SAT, the file should show market research and a reasonable basis for expecting commercial products or services.
rules.concierge: FAR 13.5 can be powerful, but only when the commercial-products/services foundation is real.

clearedBy.label: Document commercial product or commercial service support.

evidence: Market research supporting commercial product or service treatment
Commerciality analysis or determination, if required locally
Price references from the commercial marketplace or prior buys
Acquisition strategy showing why commercial procedures fit

rules.title: Authority track is unknown on an above-SAT action
rules.explanation: Above the SAT, the package should be able to explain the acquisition path before solicitation. Unknown is fine at intake, but it is not ready-to-solicit.

fixWith.label: FAR Research Tool
fixWith.description: Route the question to the right FAR part.

rules.title: Contract type is unknown on an above-SAT action
rules.explanation: Contract type affects risk, pricing, clauses, surveillance, and approval posture. Resolve it before solicitation language is built.

fixWith.label: Solicitation Builder
fixWith.description: Build the solicitation once the contract type is known.

fixWith.label: Cost and Price Analysis
fixWith.description: Review pricing and contract type risk.

rules.title: Deliverables are not defined
rules.explanation: Services packages need clear deliverables, reporting, meetings, data, or products when applicable. Undefined deliverables create evaluation and administration trouble.

clearedBy.label: Define deliverables or at least move the deliverables list into draft.

evidence: Deliverables list with due dates or frequencies
Format, content, and acceptance requirements for each deliverable
Government reviewer or acceptance official
Data, report, meeting, and product delivery assumptions

rules.title: Acceptance criteria are not defined
rules.explanation: The Government needs to know what acceptance looks like before solicitation. Vague acceptance criteria tend to become invoice, inspection, and cure-notice problems.

clearedBy.label: Define acceptance criteria or at least move them into draft.

evidence: Acceptance criteria for each major deliverable or performance outcome
Inspection method and responsible Government role
Timing for review, rejection, correction, and acceptance
Connection between acceptance and invoice approval

fixWith.label: Cure Notices
fixWith.description: See why measurable performance matters later.

rules.title: Acceptance or deliverables are only partially defined
rules.explanation: Partial is better than blank, but clean solicitation packages should say what is due, when it is due, and how the Government will accept it.

rules.title: Need date is already in the past
rules.explanation: The package should explain the real schedule pressure and reset expectations before the acquisition strategy is built around a date nobody can meet.
